messages:
Gwen (Docs): Hi all — opened PR to adjust Marlin5b model card + catalog row. Main goals: clarify scheduling/priority behavior for long-context streaming, fix compatibility table to use runtime labels, and replace an obsolete SDK snippet with streaming + fallback handling. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5173. Quick skim for customer-facing wording please.

Haruto (Runtime): Thanks Gwen. Two runtime notes: 1) use runtime labels like marlin5b-q4_k_m and marlin5b-fp16 in the compat table so customers can paste configs. 2) our scheduler may route quantized requests to a different pool when memory pressure is high — add a short note about potential soft-fallbacks and how we surface them in the stream metadata.

Felix (Bench): Pasted bench runs in the PR comments: marlin5b-q4_k_m on A10: 140-175 tok/s (batch=1, seq=4096); on T4: 48-70 tok/s (batch=1, seq=4096). Cold-starts and prompt shape change numbers a fair bit. I recommend a range and including the exact harness/seed in a hidden PR artifact.

Nora (PM): Please avoid absolutes. For the public throughput blurb: "expected throughput: ~48	68 tok/s on T4 and ~140	175 tok/s on A10 (batch=1, seq=4k); measured with the canonical benchmark prompts." Also add a short rollback/canary note for Dedicated customers (how to pin to marlin5b-fp16).

Ethan (DevEx): Reworked the Python/TS snippets to streaming and added detection for runtime_fallback metadata. Python example in the PR:
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
for chunk in client.generate_stream(prompt, model='marlin5b-q4_k_m'):
    if chunk.meta.get('runtime_fallback'):
        # record fallback and surface to user dashboards
        print('\n[fallback to ' + chunk.meta.get('runtime_variant') + ']')
    print(chunk.text, end='')
```
Can runtime confirm meta key names and whether the scheduler emits a pre-fallback event?

Haruto (Runtime): meta keys are runtime_fallback (bool) and runtime_variant (string). The scheduler emits a metadata event with runtime_fallback=true and runtime_variant set before the first fallback chunk; good to note that in the card. Also include an explicit pin example: model: 'marlin5b-fp16' for Dedicated configs.

Felix (Bench): added a sentence about batching effects: "batching can raise amortized throughput but increases p95 single-request latency; see batching guidance." Attached the bench script and docker tag in the PR.

lint-bot: docs-ci/pr-check failed  markdown-lint: duplicate-anchor-id in supported-variants table. See https://ci.redwood.dev/1489

Gwen (Docs): fixing duplicate anchors and swapping the internal runtime link to the public runtime-mapping page. Also reworded the throughput sentence per Nora. Re-requesting review.

Ethan (DevEx): pushed a short JS parity snippet and a tiny note showing the stream emits metadata before fallback:
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient();
for await (const chunk of client.generateStream({ model: 'marlin5b-q4_k_m', prompt })) {
  if (chunk.meta?.runtime_fallback) {
    console.warn('[fallback to ' + chunk.meta.runtime_variant + ']');
  }
  process.stdout.write(chunk.text);
}
```

lint-bot: docs-ci/pr-check passed on second run :white_check_mark:

Nora (PM): LGTM from PM. Gwen please add a one-line migration note for customers who used the legacy name "marlin5b" without a variant suffix. Also flag the catalog change in #docs-release after merge.

Gwen (Docs): will add the migration line and merge in ~10m unless anyone objects. I'll post the summary in #docs-release with bench caveats and the scheduler note. Thanks everyone!
